answer:
A visible backlog is one stock inside a chosen boundary, so a flat queue means only that local inflow equals local outflow. Work can keep accumulating in omitted stocks—retry buffers, operator queues, database tables—while the reported queue stays flat. The identity backlog(t+dt) = backlog(t) + arrivals(dt) - completions(dt) conserves work only inside the declared boundary; retries or entity redefinitions crossing it make attempts, unique operations and outcomes diverge. Rejecting work before the boundary can also flatten the internal queue while user-level success falls.

A stock-and-flow model must therefore make the boundary and excluded stocks explicit: state purpose, alternatives, observable metric, exclusions and validity domain; record included and excluded stocks, units, evidence status and assumptions in the model contract; and justify that omitted stocks cannot reverse the comparison. If they can, enlarge the boundary, represent them as explicit exogenous stocks or flows, or add a sensitivity case. Count offered, admitted, exited, rejected and abandoned work consistently, and record start and end backlog plus residence-time cohorts so finite-window edge effects are visible. Silently omitted stocks are a conceptual-validity defect, not a rounding error.

Evidence: V12 stock-and-flow/where-the-model-fails; V12 model-scope/from-decision-to-boundary and failure-modes-of-scope; V12 model-contract/required-structure; V07 measurement-boundary/orientation; V07 finite-window/counterexample. Confidence is high for the mechanism; whether a specific backlog is affected remains unknown because this is method evidence, not production measurement.

evidence.claim: Backlog is a stock and arrivals/completions are flows; change in backlog is their difference.
evidence.note: Observed: page gives backlog(t+dt)=backlog(t)+arrivals(dt)-completions(dt) and warns that mixing stock and flow units destroys meaning.

evidence.claim: Hidden stocks in databases, retry buffers or operator queues let a visible backlog look stable while total work grows elsewhere.
evidence.note: Observed: 'Hidden stock' failure mode; the quoted textbook sentence states the visible/stable versus total-growth divergence.

evidence.claim: A hidden stock or omitted boundary is a conceptual-model validity problem, distinct from verification and data-validity failures.
evidence.note: Observed: the page maps unit/conservation to verification, hidden stock/omitted boundary to conceptual validity, rate mismatch to data validity, citing Sargent.

evidence.claim: A model boundary separates model state from the rest of the world; omitted parts are acceptable only if they cannot change the comparison, and scope must state excluded actors, dependencies, failures and validity.
evidence.note: Observed: five-question boundary statement (purpose, alternatives, observable, excluded, validity).

evidence.claim: Boundary mismatch and omitted dependency are scope failure modes that can reverse a decision.
evidence.note: Observed: failure-mode list; boundary starting after admission is the named example.

evidence.claim: The model contract requires explicit scope (included and excluded), boundary, units, parameter evidence status, validity limits, assumptions and unknowns.
evidence.note: Observed: contract top-level fields include scope, abstraction boundary, state units, evidence status, validity_limits and unknowns.

evidence.claim: Conservation needs one boundary and consistent entity counts, with no hidden transfers, recycled jobs or redefinitions; offered, admitted and exit rates are distinct.
evidence.note: Observed: exact count balance N(t1)=N(t0)+A-D holds only under those conditions, and rejection may occur before the measured boundary.

evidence.claim: A finite observation window ending with unfinished work outside the boundary invalidates naive occupancy estimates; start/end backlog and cohorts must be recorded.
evidence.note: Observed: 1-request/5-second counterexample where full residence time extends beyond the window; engineering consequence is explicit accounting.

evidence.claim: Rejecting work before the boundary can keep internal backlog flat while user-level success falls, and retries make offered attempts exceed unique business operations.
evidence.note: Observed: synthetic 200/s offered versus 150/s completed example plus admission and retry caveats.
